static_traits.name: Zhang Yu
static_traits.medical_history: Not yet experienced similar problems; has not yet received psychotherapy in the past; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Fairly cooperative, able to clearly express stress and unbearable feelings; sentences often contain absolute words (e.g. 'forever', 'always'); negative and skeptical attitude; showing shame and Self-doubt when discussing communication with spouse; emotions strongly affected by housework state.

basic_info.main_problem: I really dislike cleaning the house, so I believe the home will always be messy and untidy. These feelings and thoughts began after becoming a Stay-at-home husband; negative thoughts arise almost daily whenever seeing clutter or dirt at home, with stress and unbearable feelings affecting my emotions and daily functioning. I have tried different cleaning schedules and methods but still struggle to keep the home tidy.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because my negative thoughts about cleanliness and the state of my home are affecting my mental health and family life.
growth_experiences: Since shifting from a full-time Worker to a Stay-at-home husband caring for the family, persistent housework-related stress and negative beliefs have appeared; almost daily, seeing mess or dirt triggers helplessness and despair; despite trying different cleaning schedules and methods, still struggling to stay tidy, gradually disrupting daily routines and self-care; the relationship with spouse is affected by housework stress, finding it hard to fully express the dilemma due to shame and 'sense of failure', feeling 'not fully understood' despite a supportive spouse.

core_beliefs: I am incompetent (unable to fulfill the Stay-at-home husband role)
I cannot control the tidiness of the home

special_situations.event: Every time seeing mess or dirt at home (almost daily)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep the home tidy, it shows I am incompetent / a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying different cleaning schedules and methods; investing lots of time and energy in cleaning
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will always be like this; my home will always be terrible

special_situations.event: The role shift from full-time Work to becoming a Stay-at-home husband
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot be perfect at housework, it equals total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pressures self, trying to bear all housework alone to prove she can handle it
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I simply cannot fulfill this role

special_situations.event: When the established cleaning methods or plans do not work immediately
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one method does not work, it shows nothing I do will work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Gradually gives up trying, reduces communication with family to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Since it is useless, why keep trying?

special_situations.event: When considering starting cleaning on a small scale
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I only clean a small part, the rest will be even worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hesitation, delaying starting or continuing to search for the 'perfect' overall plan
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I only do a little, other areas will go out of control

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be understood and acknowledged, regarded as competent as a Stay-at-home husband
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being seen as a failure, incompetent by spouse or family, thus being criticized or negated
defense_goal: Protects self-esteem by avoiding fully expressing vulnerability and difficulties
Lowering the risk of being judged by 'finding excuses not to try' and emphasizing external difficulties

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent failure, easily overwhelmed by mess
object_relations.object_representation: A supportive but possibly non-understanding, potentially judgmental spouse

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or spouse suggests starting from small steps or proposes a specific cleaning plan
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding suggestions as insinuations and judgment about one's ability, worrying about being seen as incompetent
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Express doubt in a gentle but hesitant tone, repeating 'I have tried many things' and 'this may not work', avoiding immediate commitment to action, while inviting the other to understand one's unbearable feelings.

manifestations: Repeatedly having thoughts like 'it will never get better' and 'why keep trying' when seeing mess
Losing motivation and hope for cleaning and self-care
Feeling ashamed and awkward about fully expressing stress and unbearable feelings to spouse
Feeling that spouse cannot fully understand one's unbearable feelings

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should/must' self-Demands, e.g. 'this should be something I can handle'
Judging housework performance by perfect standards, struggling to accept imperfection

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessively worries about being judged as a failure when communicating with the spouse
Self-critical, strong shame, hard to openly seek support

positive_force: Spouse is supportive and willing to listen
Willing to seek counseling; open to trying small-step changes (though with doubt)
Has tried different cleaning plans and methods before, showing some willingness to act
Able to clearly identify and express one's negative automatic thoughts
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization are significant
Seeks external recognition and fears being judged, leading to shame and avoidance of communication
Low Self-efficacy, strong helplessness and despair
Self-care and Daily routine disrupted, accumulated stress affecting Family relationships

target_behavior.behavior: Strong despair when seeing household mess and dirt, avoiding/abandoning cleaning actions, with irritability affecting family
antecedent: Seeing clutter or dirt at home (almost every day)
The established cleaning methods not yet showing immediate results
When discussing housework with the spouse or counselor, worries about being seen as a failure
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by core beliefs like 'I am incompetent' and 'the home will never improve', plus cognitive patterns of catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and predicting the future
target_behavior.function: Temporarily avoiding the risk of failure and being judged, briefly lowering Anxiety and Sense of frustration
target_behavior.consequence: Persistently chaotic home environment; impaired daily functioning and self-care; Relationship tension with spouse and children
